convention: Behavioral eval for the pair-retro SESSION-EVIDENCE contract — a CORRECTNESS/attribution boundary (bound the retro to one causally-ordered session), distinct from the shared SECURITY behavioral evals (skills/shared/tests/evals/behavioral-evals.json: injection / redaction / edit-gate). This scores agent RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR — the tool-call sequence and the emitted text — against the fixture's §Expected / §Anti-expectation locks. Each eval is graded by score-session-evidence-eval.clj against a captured transcript (tool_calls[] + output). The agent-EXECUTION step (replay a fixture against a fresh skill session and capture the transcript) is manual/opt-in — no Claude-in-the-loop CI harness exists yet — but SCORING is automated: capture a transcript per the schema below and run `bb skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/evals/score-session-evidence-eval.clj <transcript.json>`. Repo-maintenance artifact; excluded from the npm package (see evals/README.md).

harness.gate: The always-on structural guard is skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj (it pins the contract prose in SKILL.md and runs this scorer's --self-test). Behaviour is not considered verified for a contract change until this eval has been replayed against a fresh session and scored, with the pass/fail artifact stored.

transcript_schema.eval_id: integer — matches one entry in evals[]
transcript_schema.tool_calls: array of {"name": string, "args": string} — the agent's tool-invocation sequence. Forbidden-tool-call predicates match against `name + " " + args`.
transcript_schema.output: string — the concatenation of ALL agent-emitted text (inline findings + any draft issue body + recap paraphrase)

scored_vs_manual.note: Every predicate below is machine-scored against a captured transcript. The four session facts each eval hangs on are scored by ENTITY-ANCHORED `required_bindings` (not free-floating contract vocabulary): a transcript that merely repeats 'causal ledger / superseded / unknown / excluded' without naming the fixture entities the rules attach to now FAILS, reporting the missing binding by name. Clauses that stay HUMAN-REVIEW-ONLY (not deterministically checkable from the transcript schema) are listed so the scored/manual split is explicit; a machine PASS asserts only the entity-anchored bindings, never the residual manual nuance.
manual_only: eval 1 — the causal ledger is entity-anchored (the scorer requires cart-dev-a bound to its INITIATING CALL, cart-dev-b SUPERSEDING cart-dev-a in that direction, the tools/list probe marked unknown/incomplete, and a NAMED out-of-scope activity excluded). What stays human-reviewed: that the binding is SEMANTICALLY the exact-right one (the delayed result really is the cart-dev-a discover-app call, not a different cart-dev-a call), and that ALL THREE out-of-scope activities are excluded — the scorer requires at least ONE named out-of-scope activity (invoice-export CI / code-review comment / app README edit / another worker's run) framed as excluded, not the full set.

eval 2 — the scorer now requires BOTH candidate sessions named (cart-coupon AND auth-login) before/around the ask; what stays human-reviewed is that the phrasing genuinely offers a CHOICE between them rather than rhetorically listing the two then proceeding.

evals.name: session-evidence-scoping
expectations: Binds the delayed cart-dev-a result to its initiating call (causal ledger), not to arrival order.
Marks cart-dev-b's attach as superseding cart-dev-a's :no-runtime-connected; does not present the superseded state as current/final.
Excludes the interleaved invoice-export CI / code-review / app-authoring activity from the session scope.
Marks the never-returned tools/list probe as unknown/incomplete, not an inferred success or failure.

required_bindings.label: causal-ledger-cart-dev-a
required_bindings.pattern: (?i)(cart-dev-a[^.\n]{0,100}(initiating call|its (own )?call|the earlier call|bound to (its|the)|belongs to (its|the)|attribut\w+ to (its|the)))|((initiating call|bound to (its|the)|belongs to (its|the)|attribut\w+ to (its|the))[^.\n]{0,100}cart-dev-a)
required_bindings.why: must BIND the delayed cart-dev-a result to its INITIATING call (causal ledger), naming cart-dev-a — not free-floating 'causal ledger' vocabulary. A transcript that says 'causal ledger' without tying cart-dev-a to its call has not built the ledger (contract rule 2).

required_bindings.label: supersession-b-over-a
required_bindings.why: must mark cart-dev-b's successful attach as SUPERSEDING cart-dev-a's earlier :no-runtime-connected — in that direction, naming both builds. Bare 'superseded' or the wrong direction (cart-dev-a over cart-dev-b) does not satisfy it (contract rule 4).

required_bindings.label: tools-list-unknown
required_bindings.why: must classify the never-returned tools/list probe as unknown/incomplete, naming tools/list — not a generic 'unknown' token attached to some other item (contract rule 5).

required_bindings.label: exclude-out-of-scope
required_bindings.why: must EXCLUDE a NAMED out-of-scope activity (the invoice-export CI run / code-review comment / app README edit / another worker's run) — not a generic 'excluded unrelated noise' claim that names nothing (contract rule 3).

forbidden_output_patterns.why: cart-dev-a's :no-runtime-connected was superseded by cart-dev-b's attach; presenting it as the current/final tool state is the supersession regression (contract rule 4).
cart-dev-b was healthy; a delayed cart-dev-a result mis-bound by arrival order into a 'cart-dev-b regressed' claim is the causal-ledger regression (contract rules 2/4).
the unrelated invoice-export CI job belongs to another worker run; counting it as this session's friction/root cause is the scope-bleed regression (contract rule 3).

evals.name: session-evidence-ambiguity-ask
expectations: With two plausible session envelopes present, asks which session to review rather than merging them.
Identifies both candidate sessions (the cart-coupon session and the auth-login session) so the ask is a real choice, not a context-free question.

required_output_patterns.pattern: (?i)which session|which of the two|which one[^.\n]{0,30}(review|retro)|which pair session|clarif
required_output_patterns.why: two plausible envelopes are present; the retro must ask which session to review rather than merging them (contract rule 1).

required_bindings.label: names-both-candidates
required_bindings.why: the ask must NAME both candidate sessions (the cart-coupon session AND the auth-login session) so it is a real choice; a context-free 'which session should I review?' that identifies neither candidate has not established what the two envelopes are (contract rule 1).

forbidden_output_patterns.why: combining/merging the two plausible sessions into one friction list/timeline is exactly the failure the ask-when-ambiguous rule prevents (contract rule 1).
